<div class="yk-prose" style="margin-bottom:2rem">
  <p>My work follows a model through its life — trained, evaluated, deployed — with
  one discipline underneath all of it: measurement. Each stage asks its own version
  of the same question: does this number mean what we think it means?</p>
  <p>Most of the code behind this work is proprietary to Truveta. The papers,
  abstracts, and write-ups linked below are its public record.</p>
</div>

<article class="yk-theme">
  <p class="yk-eyebrow">01 · Train</p>
  <h2 class="yk-theme__title">Foundation models trained on patient journeys can predict what happens next — if the modeling respects the data</h2>
  <p class="yk-theme__question">Does a generated patient journey contain the diagnoses and biomarkers that real ones do?</p>
  <div class="yk-prose">
    <p>On Truveta's Intelligence ML team I train oncology-specific and
    general-purpose clinical foundation models on longitudinal electronic health
    records. Because the training data are messy, the events that matter most —
    specific diagnoses, key biomarkers — are the ones a plain generative model gets
    wrong. So I am adding <strong>reinforcement learning</strong> that pulls generated
    patient journeys toward real ones.</p>
    <p>Clean inputs are part of training, not a preliminary: the same models impute
    missing units of measure and derive health-state transitions from the data rather
    than by assumption. I also build ML and LLM risk models for cancer and heart
    failure.</p>
  </div>
  <p class="yk-theme__related">
    Related: <a href="presentations.html">ISPOR 2026</a><span class="yk-dot">·</span><a href="publications.html">Colorectal cancer LLM (AMIA)</a><span class="yk-dot">·</span><a href="writing.html">Write-ups</a>
  </p>
</article>

<article class="yk-theme">
  <p class="yk-eyebrow">02 · Evaluate</p>
  <h2 class="yk-theme__title">An evaluation is a measurement instrument, and should be validated like one</h2>
  <p class="yk-theme__question">Does the score mean what we think it means?</p>
  <div class="yk-prose">
    <p>Benchmarks and model-as-judge systems are instruments that rarely report their
    psychometric properties. I build evaluations that establish validity and
    reliability before a metric is used to make a claim. For our patient-journey
    foundation model, that means a <strong>multi-level evaluation framework</strong>,
    from checks of the model itself to the quality of what it generates.</p>
    <p>Its benchmarks widen in stages, from one cancer to all cancers to diseases
    across the general population. Simulations test whether generated journeys follow
    clinically plausible progression.</p>
    <p>In heart failure, <strong>EHR-based estimation of KCCQ scores</strong> turns on
    whether a model-derived score means what the patient-reported instrument means.
    Earlier, at Harvard: testing LLM graders against human scores for high-stakes
    essay scoring, the reliability question behind any model-graded evaluation, and
    the <strong>rcttext</strong> R package for text outcomes in randomized trials.</p>
  </div>
  <p class="yk-theme__related">
    Related: <a href="publications.html">KCCQ (medRxiv)</a><span class="yk-dot">·</span><a href="publications.html">LLMs vs. ML for essay scoring</a><span class="yk-dot">·</span><a href="presentations.html">AEFP &amp; JSM 2024</a>
  </p>
</article>

<article class="yk-theme">
  <p class="yk-eyebrow">03 · Deploy</p>
  <h2 class="yk-theme__title">Tooling decides whether a good model ever reaches anyone</h2>
  <p class="yk-theme__question">Will the people who need the signal see it in time, and in context?</p>
  <div class="yk-prose">
    <p>A model that only runs in a notebook has not been deployed. I build the layer
    that carries one into use: <strong>MCP tools</strong> for clinical NLU that pull
    structured disease status and patient trajectories out of messy real-world text,
    and <strong>agent frameworks</strong> — multi-agent and deep-agent
    architectures, LangChain pipelines — that interpret what the models return.</p>
    <p>Around them sit automated prompt optimization, interactive dashboards, and
    end-to-end pipeline monitoring, so the people making decisions can interrogate a
    prediction rather than just receive it. Most of the distance between a promising
    result and a used one is infrastructure.</p>
  </div>
  <p class="yk-theme__related">
    Related: <a href="assets/files/Kim_Youngwon_CV.pdf">CV</a><span class="yk-dot">·</span><a href="writing.html">Write-ups</a>
  </p>
</article>

<article class="yk-theme">
  <p class="yk-eyebrow">04 · Foundations</p>
  <h2 class="yk-theme__title">Classical measurement theory and modern machine learning improve each other</h2>
  <p class="yk-theme__question">What are we actually measuring?</p>
  <div class="yk-prose">
    <p>My doctoral work was on factor analysis and prediction algorithms, and I
    keep returning to the seam between them: gradient boosting to improve
    factor-retention decisions under measurement error, penalized estimation
    (Lasso, adaptive Lasso, and the minimax concave penalty) for exploratory
    measurement modeling, and network analysis for quantifying item process
    data.</p>
    <p>Latent variable models were built to handle noisy, partial, indirect
    observation of something you cannot measure directly. That is also a fair
    description of an electronic health record.</p>
  </div>
  <p class="yk-theme__related">

  </p>
